issues.t: Engine damage from over-revving on a missed downshift
issues.sym: A sudden loud mechanical noise after a downshift, followed by misfiring, ticking, low power, or an engine that will not run right.
issues.why: These engines rev very high. Grabbing the wrong gear on a downshift (for example, second instead of fourth) can spin the engine far past redline, which can bend valves or damage the valvetrain. Oil starvation in hard track driving can also hurt the engine.
issues.next: If you suspect an over-rev, stop driving and have a compression and leak-down test done. When buying a used S2000, ask a Honda-savvy shop to check for this.

issues.t: Burning oil on early cars
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes a quart every 1,000 miles or worse, and you may see a puff of blue smoke at high revs.
issues.why: Early 2.0L cars are known for using oil, especially when driven hard into the high-rpm VTEC range. Crankcase ventilation and piston oil-jet design play a part.
issues.next: Check the dipstick at every fill-up and top up as needed. Running these engines low on oil is a common cause of failure. An oil catch can or updated oil-jet bolts help some owners.

issues.t: Cracked valve spring retainers
issues.sym: Ticking or clattering from the top of the engine, a misfire, or a cracked retainer found when the valves are adjusted.
issues.why: The valve spring retainers used on early engines were weaker than the later design and can crack, especially after over-revs. A broken retainer can drop a valve into the engine.
issues.next: Ask for the retainers to be inspected at the next valve adjustment. Many owners upgrade to the later 2.2L-style retainers as a precaution.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner rattle
issues.sym: A rattle or a sound like a playing card in bicycle spokes from the engine, often at idle or around 2,000-3,000 rpm.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner wears and stops holding the chain tight, so the chain slaps against its guides.
issues.next: Have the noise checked soon. Replacing the tensioner is a fairly small job compared with the damage a loose chain can cause.

issues.t: Grinding or notchy shifts into second gear
issues.sym: Gears grind or feel notchy, mostly going into second or third and worst when the car is cold.
issues.why: Wear on the synchronizers (the parts that match gear speeds before they engage) and old gear oil cause grinding. Honda issued service bulletins for grinding on upshifts and gear clash between first and second.
issues.next: Change the manual transmission fluid with Honda MTF first and let the car warm up before shifting hard. If grinding stays, a shop may need to replace synchronizers.

issues.t: Transmission pops out of gear
issues.sym: The shifter jumps back to neutral on its own, usually from second or fourth gear, often under acceleration or deceleration.
issues.why: Honda issued service bulletins for the later S2000 transmission jumping out of second and fourth gear due to internal wear in the shift parts.
issues.next: Hold the lever lightly and do not keep driving it this way; it can leave you without drive at a bad moment. Ask a Honda dealer to check the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Buzzing or noisy clutch pedal
issues.sym: A buzz from the pedal area or transmission, especially when slowing down, or a clutch pedal that feels notchy or noisy.
issues.why: The clutch release bearing and clutch parts transmit a vibration that can be heard in the cabin. Honda issued service bulletins for decel buzz and a noisy clutch pedal, and later redesigned the clutch.
issues.next: This is usually harmless. If the noise grows, or the clutch starts slipping, have the clutch inspected.

issues.t: Torn or worn convertible top
issues.sym: Tears in the soft top, often at the lock handle or right rear corner, plus water dripping into the cabin in rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The fabric folds at the same points every time the top goes down and wears through over the years. Honda issued bulletins for tears on 2005 and newer tops.
issues.next: Small tears can be patched with fabric glue and a patch. Avoid automatic car washes. A worn top should be replaced before water damages the interior and electronics.

issues.t: Plastic rear window creased, scratched or cloudy
issues.sym: The clear plastic rear window looks cloudy, yellow, creased or scratched, and it is hard to see out the back.
issues.why: Early cars used a plastic rear window that creases when the top is lowered, scratches easily and clouds up from road grime. Later cars got a glass window.
issues.next: Clean only with soft cloths and plastic-safe cleaner. A badly damaged window is replaced with the top or upgraded to a glass window.

issues.t: Water leaks from the soft top in car washes
issues.sym: Water drips into the cabin after an automatic car wash or pressure washing.
issues.why: High-pressure water can get past the top's seals and can damage the top itself on early cars.
issues.next: Hand-wash the car. If it leaks in normal rain too, have the top seals and drains checked.

issues.t: Creaks and rattles from the closed top
issues.sym: Squeaks, creaks or wind noise from the soft top when it is up and you drive over bumps.
issues.why: The top's pivot points dry out and the lock handles can have play. Honda's fix was lubrication and shims at the lock handles.
issues.next: Lubricate the pivot points and ask a shop to shim the latches. Hard-top style strikers also help some owners.

issues.t: Heater blower motor overheats and blows its fuse
issues.sym: The fan stops working, often suddenly, and the fuse is found blown. In bad cases the fan wheel melts.
issues.why: The blower motor's cooling hose gets clogged, so the motor runs hot. Honda issued a service bulletin on this.
issues.next: Replace the fuse once; if it blows again, have the blower and its cooling hose checked.

issues.t: A/C water dripping into passenger footwell
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the passenger side, especially after using the air conditioning.
issues.why: Condensation from the A/C leaks through a seam at the bottom of the heater housing instead of draining outside.
issues.next: Have the lower seam of the heater housing resealed. Dry the carpet to prevent mold.

issues.t: Whistling from the vents when A/C is on
issues.sym: A high whistle from the dash vents whenever the air conditioning runs.
issues.why: The A/C expansion valve, which meters refrigerant into the evaporator, can vibrate and whistle.
issues.next: It is mostly an annoyance. A shop can replace the expansion valve if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed EVAP solenoid
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with an EVAP code, especially in areas that salt their roads in winter.
issues.why: A solenoid in the fuel vapor (EVAP) system corrodes and fails.
issues.next: Have the code read. It does not hurt the engine but will fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Check engine light after long drives (software)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on after more than about four hours of driving, with no change in how the car runs.
issues.why: A software glitch in the engine computer (PCM) sets a false code on long trips.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer check for and install the software update.

issues.t: Air/fuel sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes such as P1172 or P2A00, sometimes with poorer fuel economy.
issues.why: Moisture in the exhaust when the engine is cold can damage the air/fuel (front oxygen) sensor. Honda issued service bulletins for this.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the sensor replaced. Driving a long time with a bad sensor can hurt fuel economy and the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Hesitation under hard acceleration
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or hesitates for a moment when you floor it, then picks up again.
issues.why: Honda issued service bulletins for intermittent hesitation under hard acceleration on these years, addressed with diagnosis and updates.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have a Honda-savvy shop check for the bulletin fix and for ignition or fuel problems.

issues.t: Clicking or creaking from the rear axles
issues.sym: A click or creak from the rear when pulling away in first or reverse, or a grunt at low speed.
issues.why: The rear axle nuts were under-tightened from the factory spec, letting the axle shift in the hub. Honda updated the torque spec and issued bulletins for rear creaks.
issues.next: Have the rear axle nuts torqued to Honda's updated spec. It is a quick, cheap fix.

issues.t: Popping noise from front upper control arm
issues.sym: A pop or clunk from the front of the car over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: Honda issued a service bulletin for a popping sound at the front upper control arm mount.
issues.next: Have the front suspension mounts checked against the bulletin.

issues.t: Dashboard bubbling or wrinkling
issues.sym: The dash top develops bubbles, blisters or wrinkles, usually in hot climates.
issues.why: The dash covering separates from the panel underneath with heat over time.
issues.next: Use a sunshade. Fixing it means replacing the dash panel.

issues.t: Odometer overstates mileage
issues.sym: The speedometer reads a bit high and the odometer adds miles faster than you really drove.
issues.why: A class action found certain 2002-2006 Hondas overstated mileage. Honda extended warranties to make up for the extra miles.
issues.next: Compare against GPS speed. Ask a Honda dealer whether your car got the mileage-related warranty extension.

issues.t: VSA stability control module failure
issues.sym: The VSA (stability control) and ABS warning lights come on and stay on.
issues.why: The VSA control unit, which runs ABS and stability control, can fail.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but ABS and stability control may not. Have the codes read by a shop with Honda software.

issues.t: Seat belt retractor can lock up (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt that will not pull out of its retractor, so it cannot be worn.
issues.why: The seat belt retractor can deform and lock. Recall 00V316 replaces the seat belt assembly.
issues.next: Check that both belts pull out and retract smoothly. Ask a Honda dealer to confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Seat belts don't retract with the top down (recall)
issues.sym: With the top down and the seats all the way back, the belts stay loose instead of pulling snug.
issues.why: The folded top cover gets in the way of the belts. Recall 00V016 replaces the convertible top cover.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Taillight side reflectors don't meet standards (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you would notice; the side marker and reflector lenses in the taillights are not bright enough to meet federal rules.
issues.why: The taillight lens design did not meet the federal standard. Honda recalled the cars to fix it.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer to check whether the recall was completed.
